test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 English Previous Paper 1 (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. There are others who claim that they have never been so well connected.

B. However, such social networking sites help us to keep in touch with old friends or make new ones.

C. Whether or not Facebook friendships are lasting is debatable.

D. Some people believe that real friendships are collapsing in modern times.
solution:
The correct answer is 'DACB.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'D' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "**some people who believe that ****real friendships are collapsing**". Hence, 'D' is the first part.
 
• Sentence A will come after D as it is giving information about the other people who** ****claim that they have never been so well connected**.
 
• Sentence C will come after A as it raises questions about the Facebook friendship.
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding part as it further explains how** ****social networking sites like Facebook help us to keep in touch with old friends or make new ones**.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *Some people believe that real friendships are collapsing in modern times. There are others who claim that they have never been so well connected. Whether or not Facebook friendships are lasting is debatable. However, such social networking sites help us to keep in touch with old friends or make new ones.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
